Coordinate-free by rule: it names the gene, the protein and the variant classes, never a position. Revised, never edited: bump `version` and append to `history`.

gene.protein: BubR1 (mitotic checkpoint serine/threonine-protein kinase BUB1 beta)

alleles.label: stop
alleles.reading: null allele: truncates BubR1 upstream of the C-terminal kinase domain

alleles.label: missense
alleles.reading: presumed hypomorph: a partly working copy inside the C-terminal kinase domain (CDD cd14029)

mechanism.class: loss-of-function, hypomorphic (compound heterozygote: one null allele + one partly functional allele)
mechanism.status: inferred from Track 1; the trans configuration is what the oracle tests (H009, testing)
mechanism.pathway: spindle assembly checkpoint (SAC) - mitotic checkpoint complex (MCC) formation and APC/C-CDC20 inhibition
mechanism.immediate_effect: reduced BubR1 abundance and checkpoint signalling; weakened kinetochore-microtubule attachment error correction
downstream: mosaic aneuploidy in dividing tissues (variegated: different chromosomes in different cells)
aneuploidy-associated proteotoxic and metabolic stress in surviving cells
cancer predisposition: rhabdomyosarcoma, Wilms tumour, leukaemia (MVA1 spectrum)
growth restriction (short stature, failure to thrive, IUGR), nephrocalcinosis
mechanism.complete_loss: embryonic lethal in mouse and human - full inhibition of BubR1 is not a therapeutic direction

literature.role: Hanks 2004: biallelic BUB1B mutations cause MVA with cancer predisposition; truncating + missense genotypes
Suijkerbuijk 2010: MVA patient cells have strongly reduced BUBR1 and a weakened SAC; missense alleles act as hypomorphs
BubR1 insufficiency, aneuploidy and premature ageing in the mouse hypomorph

repurposing_directions.name: SAC reinforcement / chromosomal-instability reduction
repurposing_directions.rationale: compensate for reduced BubR1 signalling; agents that prolong mitotic checkpoint arrest or stabilise kinetochore-microtubule attachments

repurposing_directions.name: aneuploidy-selective stress exploitation
repurposing_directions.rationale: aneuploid cells carry proteotoxic and energy stress; published aneuploidy-selective killing (AICAR-class energy stress, chloroquine-class autophagy stress, HSP90/HSF1 axis)

repurposing_directions.name: proteostasis / BubR1 stabilisation for a hypomorph
repurposing_directions.rationale: a partly working protein can be stabilised or its turnover slowed; explore APC/C, deacetylase and chaperone routes; note BubR1 acetylation regulates its stability

repurposing_directions.name: cancer prevention in the MVA1 tumour context
repurposing_directions.rationale: the child's presenting tumour is rhabdomyosarcoma; approved agents with a chemoprevention or surveillance rationale in aneuploidy-driven tumours

constraints.eligibility: market-approved drugs only (challenge rules, Track 2 definition); ChEMBL max_phase 4 or an FDA label is the evidence of approval

columns.name: symbol
columns.description: the gene, by its approved HGNC symbol — e.g. BUB1B, AURKB

columns.name: role
columns.description: 'seed' when the mechanism card named this gene itself, 'pathway' when the Reactome expansion added it as a member of a matching pathway

columns.name: direction_ids
columns.description: which of the card's repurposing directions (D1-D4) this gene serves; empty for a gene the pathway expansion added under no particular direction

columns.name: pathways
columns.description: the Reactome pathway ids (R-HSA-...) that put this gene in the target set

columns.name: uniprot
columns.description: the UniProt accession of the protein the gene codes for — the stable id drug databases key their target records on

catalog.method: Seed targets are the union of the card's per-direction seed_targets, in card order. Pathway targets are every human ReferenceGeneProduct participating in a Reactome pathway that (a) contains the card's UniProt accession, per /data/mapping/UniProt/{acc}/pathways?species=9606, and (b) whose displayName matches /checkpoint|kinetochore|mitotic/i. A gene that is already a seed keeps role 'seed'. The pattern is a parameter of the expansion, not a constant: a different mechanism card passes its own.

columns.name: drug_name
columns.description: the molecule, by its preferred name (upper case in ChEMBL)

columns.name: drug_id
columns.description: its ChEMBL id — the stable key across all three drug sources

columns.name: target_symbol
columns.description: the gene from targets.tsv this drug acts on

columns.name: target_role
columns.description: that gene's role: 'seed' or 'pathway' — see targets.role

columns.name: direction_ids
columns.description: the card directions the target serves (D1-D4)

columns.name: source
columns.description: which public sources reported this drug-target pair: opentargets, chembl, dgidb. Several means several agreed, which is corroboration, not a duplicate

columns.name: interaction_or_moa
columns.description: how the drug acts on the target, in the source's own words — a ChEMBL mechanism of action, or a DGIdb interaction type

columns.name: action_type
columns.description: the direction of the effect: INHIBITOR, AGONIST, ANTAGONIST, and so on

columns.name: max_phase
columns.description: the furthest clinical trial phase this molecule has reached, 1-4; 4 means market-approved. Empty when no source stated one

columns.name: approved
columns.description: market-approved somewhere: ChEMBL max_phase 4, or an Open Targets clinical stage of APPROVAL, or DGIdb's own approved flag. This is the Track 2 filter

columns.name: fda_label
columns.description: the openFDA label id, when one was found. **Empty means not checked** — only approved drugs were queried — which is not the same as 'no label exists'

columns.name: pmids
columns.description: PubMed ids the source cited for this drug-target pair

columns.name: first_approval
columns.description: the year the drug was first approved, per ChEMBL

columns.name: atc
columns.description: ATC codes — the WHO's therapeutic classification of the drug, e.g. L01 for antineoplastics; useful for grouping candidates by what they are normally for

catalog.method: For every target in targets.tsv: Open Targets drugAndClinicalCandidates (a search for the exact approved symbol, then the target), ChEMBL mechanisms for every human target whose components declare that gene symbol, and one batched DGIdb interactions query over the whole symbol list. Rows are deduped on (drug_name.lower(), target_symbol); a row merged from several sources lists all of them in `source`. max_phase, first_approval and atc are then filled from one batched ChEMBL molecule lookup over every ChEMBL id any source produced, which also replaces a bare ChEMBL id with the preferred name. `approved` is the disjunction of ChEMBL max_phase == 4, an Open Targets clinical stage of APPROVAL, and DGIdb's own approved flag. openFDA is then queried once per approved drug name; `fda_label` is empty for a row that was never checked, which is not the same statement as false.

columns.description: which snapshot query returned this study — the disease query, or a per-drug query against the tumour context. Lets a disease hit be told from a drug hit without re-running anything

catalog.method: Two query families, both derived from the card: one cond= query for the card's disease name with any parenthetical gloss stripped, and one intr=<drug> cond=<tumour context> query per approved candidate drug name. The disease query walks up to 3 pages of 100; the per-drug queries take the first page only. A study matching two queries appears once per query, tagged in the `query` column. Every query and its hit count, including the zeros, is listed in snapshot.json.

catalog.method: Four query families over PubMed E-utilities: <gene> AND (repurposing OR inhibitor OR <anchor>); <pathway head phrase> AND drug; per direction, the direction name with its slash-separated segments OR'd, AND <anchor>; and the PMIDs the card itself cites. <anchor> is the last alphabetic word of the card's disease name. The direction family is the weak one: a long descriptive name becomes a long AND-chain and can match nothing. Those zeros are recorded in snapshot.json rather than papered over with a looser query.

register.statement: The disease mechanism in this proband is hypomorphic loss of BUB1B function: one null allele (stop_gained, exon 17 of 23) plus one partly functional allele (kinase-domain missense), leaving reduced BubR1 and a leaky spindle assembly checkpoint; there is no gain-of-function or dominant-negative component.
register.prediction: Public sources agree with the shape: ClinVar and the literature classify BUB1B MVA1 as autosomal recessive loss of function; every reported MVA1 genotype combines a null with a hypomorph or two hypomorphs; no BUB1B variant is annotated dominant or gain-of-function in ClinVar/OMIM; Reactome places BUB1B in the mitotic spindle checkpoint pathway.
register.refuted_by: Any ClinVar or OMIM record of a dominant or gain-of-function BUB1B mechanism, functional evidence that kinase-domain missense alleles act as dominant negatives, or the oracle returning no match for the BUB1B pair (which would make the mechanism argument moot).
